topPRs.title: feat(ops): add read-only check of chain TOML roles/addresses against onchain state
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
## Problem

Nothing checks that the hand-maintained `[roles]` and `[addresses]` in `superchain/configs/<superchain>/<chain>.toml` still match the chain's actual onchain state. The daily-codegen job fetches onchain data, but it only writes `superchain/extra/addresses/addresses.json` and `chainList.*`. When the two disagree, nothing fails.

Example: Unichain's L1 ProxyAdmin owner changed onchain on 2026-09-13 from `0x6d5B183F538ABB8572F5cD17109c617b994D5833` to `0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A`. Daily codegen picked up the new owner in `addresses.json` (#1335). `superchain/configs/mainnet/unichain.toml` still has the old owner, and no check caught it.

## Design

- New tool `ops/cmd/check_onchain_configs`. It uses the same path as codegen to fetch data: `manage.FetchChains` (op-fetcher) and then `config.CreateAddressesWithRolesFromFetcher`. It then compares each chain's TOML against that data with `manage.DiffChainAgainstOnchain`.
- The tool only reads. It never writes TOML or any other file.
- It compares only fields that are present in the TOML, in both `[roles]` and `[addresses]`. Many configs list only some fields (for example, most list only `ProxyAdminOwner` under `[roles]`), and missing fields are skipped.
- Each mismatch prints one line per chain and field, for example:
  `[NOTOK] mainnet/unichain (chain 130): [roles] ProxyAdminOwner: toml=0x6d5B… onchain=0x5a0A…`
  The tool exits non-zero if any chain has a mismatch.
- If the fetcher returns the zero address for a field the TOML sets, the tool prints `[ WARN]` and does not fail. A zero address means the fetcher could not find the field, not that the TOML is wrong. Today this happens with `DisputeGameFactoryProxy` on several chains whose fault-proof wiring the fetcher doesn't detect.
- CI: the new `check-onchain-configs` job runs in the scheduled `daily-codegen` workflow. It runs alongside codegen, uses the same contexts and RPC secrets, and sends a Slack alert to `#notify-ci` and @protocol-oncall on failure, the same way `daily-codegen` does. I did not add it to per-PR CI. Onchain state changes without any PR, and right now the check would fail every PR (see below). Once the existing mismatches are fixed, it can also go into the `main` workflow.
- You can run it locally with `just check-onchain-configs <sepolia_rpc>,<mainnet_rpc>`. It also accepts `--chain-ids` and `--superchains`.

## Current state on main: this check will fail

I ran the check against public RPCs (publicnode). It reports 14 chains that disagree with onchain state, including mainnet/unichain. A separate PR fixes `unichain.toml`. The other chains need their own fixes, so this job will fail until all of them are updated. I spot-checked a few results by calling `owner()` directly on the ProxyAdmin. The onchain values also match what `addresses.json` already has.

| chain | field | toml | onchain |

| mainnet/unichain (130) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x6d5B183F538ABB8572F5cD17109c617b994D5833 | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A |
| mainnet/hashkeychain (177) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x441F31C4cdf772558D4EA31f3114de59aE145E7c | 0x3228F00FbFD0e1F4c282601c489664B10932C40f |
| mainnet/metal (1750) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 |
| mainnet/mint (185) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 | 0x3c54Be307E15258E51d42E585831bD7E04BBc03b |
| mainnet/mode (34443) | ProxyAdminOwner | 0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A | 0x4a4962275DF8C60a80d3a25faEc5AA7De116A746 |

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and `golangci-lint` (v1.64.8) pass on the changed packages in `ops`. The `go test ./internal/manage/ ./internal/config/` tests pass, including the new `TestDiffChainAgainstOnchain`.
- I ran `go run ./cmd/check_onchain_configs` against public Sepolia and mainnet RPCs. It produced the results above, and `--chain-ids` filtering works.
- I have not run the new CircleCI job. It will first run on the next `build_daily` schedule or a `daily_codegen_dispatch` trigger.

topPRs.title: fix(ops): convert deploy-config hardfork offsets to absolute times when staging
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Staging a new chain copied the deploy config's `L2Genesis*TimeOffset` values straight into the registry's absolute `*_time` fields. A future offset such as 86400 was therefore staged as Unix time 86400, so every registry-driven client would treat that fork as active from genesis. Non-zero offsets now have the L2 genesis time added, matching op-chain-ops' `offsetToUpgradeTime`. A zero offset still means "active at genesis" and is stored as 0.

Chains added with nil or 0 offsets, the usual case, stage exactly as before. Genesis validation could not catch the wrong times, because fork times do not affect the genesis hash. The existing unit test had locked in the raw copy and is updated.

Reported by Cantina Apex (OPTI1-115).

topPRs.title: fix(configs): sync stale roles and addresses with onchain state
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Updates 13 chain TOMLs whose hand-maintained `[roles]`/`[addresses]` values no longer match onchain state. These are the remaining mismatches reported by `check_onchain_configs` in #1362; `mainnet/unichain` is handled separately in #1361.

Each new value matches `superchain/extra/addresses/addresses.json` (written from L1 by daily codegen, last run in #1360). No other `[roles]` or `[addresses]` field in these 13 files differs from `addresses.json`. No generated file references the old values, so codegen output is unchanged.

## For reviewers

- mainnet metal, mode and zora (and their Sepolia counterparts) still have `governed_by_optimism = true`, but their ProxyAdmin is no longer owned by the standard L1PAO. This PR doesn't change that flag. Someone should decide whether it's still accurate.
- cyber and funki now point to a different `DisputeGameFactoryProxy`. Their other fault-proof addresses in the TOML already match `addresses.json`.

## Testing

- Compared every `[roles]`/`[addresses]` field in the 13 files against `addresses.json`; only these 13 differed, and all now match.
- I didn't make a fresh RPC call for this PR. The values come from daily codegen and the #1362 public-RPC run, and those two sources agree.

topPRs.title: fix(unichain): update mainnet ProxyAdminOwner to the OP-governed L1PAO
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
Updates `[roles].ProxyAdminOwner` in `superchain/configs/mainnet/unichain.toml` from the Unichain 3-of-3 (`0x6d5B183F538ABB8572F5cD17109c617b994D5833`) to the standard OP-governed L1PAO (`0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A`).

- [superchain-ops eth/069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/tasks/eth/069-unichain-l1-ownership-transfers/README.md) (executed) transferred the L1 `ProxyAdmin` and `DisputeGameFactoryProxy` to the L1PAO. [eth/070](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/tasks/eth/070-unichain-l2pao-transfer/README.md) moved the L2 `ProxyAdmin` to its alias.
- Verified on-chain on 2026-10-09: `owner()` on `ProxyAdmin` `0x3B73Fa8d82f511A3caE17B5a26E4E1a2d5E2f2A4` and `DisputeGameFactoryProxy` `0x2F12d621a16e2d3285929C9996f478508951dFe4` returns `0x5a0Aae59D09fccBdDb6C6CcEB07B7279367C3d2A`.
- `superchain/extra/addresses/addresses.json` already has this value from the daily codegen run ([#1335](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1335)). Only the hand-maintained TOML was stale, and no CI check compares the two.

No codegen run needed; generated files are unchanged.

Prompted by: @mds1
